normative_extracts.quote: The relational pseudo-class :has() takes a relative selector list as an argument and matches if any of the relative selectors match at least one element when anchored against the subject.

engine_internals.mechanism_summary: Engines attach :has() invalidation flags to ancestors/siblings so DOM mutations only re-evaluate affected subjects instead of scanning the whole tree.

production_failures.symptom: Style recalculation spikes when typing into an input inside a huge form
production_failures.root_cause: Using :root:has(input:invalid) forces document-wide invalidation checks on every keystroke.
production_failures.mitigation: Scope :has() to the nearest container (.field:has(:invalid)) instead of :root or body.

production_failures.symptom: :has() fails to match pseudo-elements like ::before or ::after
production_failures.root_cause: Per CSS Selectors L4, pseudo-elements are invalid inside :has() arguments.
production_failures.mitigation: Match real DOM elements or state pseudo-classes (:checked, :focus-within, :empty) inside :has().
